title: Restriction-form transition of simultaneous derived direct image
statement:
Let $u:V\to W$ be any morphism of schemes, and use small representatives of their pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $B_1\leftarrow B_2\leftarrow\cdots$ be any strict tower of sheaves of commutative rings on $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, put $C_n=u^{-1}B_n$, and use the induced tower on $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $\mathscr S(B),\mathscr S(C)$ be the strict semilinear module-system categories, with their ordinary unbounded derived categories and the simultaneous direct image $G=Ru_{*,\bullet}$ of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Write $G_n=Ru_{*,B_n}$, and for $m\ge n$ write $r^W_{m,n},r^V_{m,n}$ for exact restriction of scalars along $B_m\to B_n,C_m\to C_n$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Let $\delta_{m,n}:G_m r^V_{m,n}\xrightarrow{\sim}r^W_{m,n}G_n$ be the inverse of the canonical ring-sheaf-change comparison $d$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction]. For $N\in D(\mathscr S(C))$, let $a^N_{m,n}:N_m\to r^V_{m,n}N_n$ and $a^{GN}_{m,n}:(GN)_m\to r^W_{m,n}(GN)_n$ be its actual derived restriction-form transitions. Under the canonical natural evaluation isomorphisms $e_nG\cong G_ne_n$, one has
$$a^{GN}_{m,n}=\delta_{m,n,N_n}\circ G_m(a^N_{m,n}).$$
The formula is natural in $N$ and includes $m=n$. Its comparison has this normalization: for a K-injective $C_n$-complex $I$ and a K-injective replacement $r^V_{m,n}I\to H$ over $C_m$, $\delta_{m,n,QI}$ is the inverse of the class of $u_*r^V_{m,n}I=r^W_{m,n}u_*I\to u_*H$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. No flatness of the tower maps, normalization of $N$, or preservation of K-injectives by restriction or evaluation is assumed. Write $T=-\otimes^L_{B_m}B_n$ and $S=-\otimes^L_{C_m}C_n$, with their exact restriction-of-scalars right adjoints [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Let $b:TG_m\to G_nS$ be the coefficient-extension mate specified in [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. For every $M\in D(C_m)$, $L\in D(C_n)$ and $a:M\to r^V_{m,n}L$, the same comparison satisfies the scalar-transpose identity
$$\bigl(\delta_{m,n,L}\circ G_m(a)\bigr)^\sharp=G_n(a^\sharp)\circ b_M.$$
Here sharp denotes precisely the two coefficient extension/restriction adjunction bijections. Thus the scalar mate of the resolution-normalized restriction comparison is the specified system coefficient mate.

source.place: Tag 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition), normalization of the two coefficient factorizations. The restriction-form transition identity is the implicit mate-identification prerequisite using the existing coherent-section theorem.

proof.text: Fix $m\ge n$, abbreviate $p=r^W_{m,n}$ and $q=r^V_{m,n}$, and put $F_i=u^{-1}:D(B_i)\to D(C_i)$, with right adjoint $G_i$. The ring-change theorem applies with $R_W=B_m$, $S_W=B_n$, $R_V=C_m$, $S_V=C_n$, and both coefficient identifications the identity: its compatibility equation is exactly $C_m\to C_n=u^{-1}(B_m\to B_n)$. It gives $d:pG_n\xrightarrow{\sim}G_mq$ and hence $\delta=d^{-1}$. The scalar adjunctions are $T\dashv p$ and $S\dashv q$ on the ordinary unbounded derived categories. All four sites/ringed topoi in this coefficient square are small in the prescribed universe.

Consider the two equal ringed-topos composites $(V,C_n)\to(W,B_m)$, factored through $(V,C_m)$ and through $(W,B_n)$. Their composite left adjoints are $SF_m$ and $F_nT$, and their composite right adjoints are $G_mq$ and $pG_n$. Write $\alpha:SF_m\xrightarrow{\sim}F_nT$ for the canonical pullback comparison between the two factorizations (built from the pullback-composition comparisons $c_{f,g}$) and $\chi=\alpha^{-1}$. Since each $\kappa$ is adjunction-compatible, both composite adjunctions are identified with the adjunction of the composite, so $d:pG_n\to G_mq$, the direct-image comparison of the two factorizations, is the right-adjoint conjugate of $\alpha$; hence $\delta=d^{-1}$ is the conjugate of $\chi$. It remains to see that $\alpha$ is the coefficient comparison used to define $b$, which the normalized geometric interface fixes as the $S\dashv q$ transpose of the identity-on-underlying-sheaves comparison $u^{-1}p=qu^{-1}$, namely of $F_m(\eta^T_P):F_mP\to qF_nTP$. Check on a K-flat complex $P$ of $B_m$-modules with flat terms, where both are computed termwise. Since $C_i=u^{-1}B_i$, module pullback is $u^{-1}$, and $c_{f,g}$ makes $\alpha_P$ the class of $u^{-1}P\otimes_{C_m}C_n\to u^{-1}(P\otimes_{B_m}B_n)$, $x\otimes\lambda\mapsto\lambda\cdot u^{-1}(x\otimes1)$. Normalizations (1) and (2) of the coefficient adjunction compute that transpose as $x\otimes\lambda\mapsto\lambda\cdot u^{-1}(\eta^T_P(x))=\lambda\cdot u^{-1}(x\otimes1)$: the same map. Thus $b$ is the mate of $\chi:F_nT\to SF_m$.

Write $\eta^T:1\to pT$, $\epsilon^S:Sq\to1$ for the scalar unit and counit and $\eta^i,\epsilon^i$ for those of $F_i\dashv G_i$. By the definition of mate, $b:TG_m\to G_nS$ is the mate of $\chi:F_nT\to SF_m$ under $F_m\dashv G_m$ and $F_n\dashv G_n$:
$$b=G_nS\epsilon^m\circ G_n\chi G_m\circ\eta^nTG_m.$$
The composite adjunctions of step 2 have units and counits as in the mate-pasting theorem: $\eta^{F_nT}=p\eta^nT\circ\eta^T$ and $\epsilon^{SF_m}=\epsilon^S\circ S\epsilon^mq$. Hence the conjugate of $\chi$, which is $\delta$ by step 2, is
$$\delta=pG_n\epsilon^S\circ pG_nS\epsilon^mq\circ pG_n\chi G_mq\circ p\eta^nTG_mq\circ\eta^TG_mq,$$
and the middle three factors are $p(bq)$. So, at every $L\in D(C_n)$,
$$\delta_L=pG_n(\epsilon^S_L)\circ p(b_{qL})\circ\eta^T_{G_mqL}.$$
This is a direct unit/counit calculation; it does not assert that taking mates preserves invertibility for an arbitrary square.

For $a:M\to qL$, step 3 and naturality of $\eta^T$ give
$$\delta_LG_m(a)=p\bigl(G_n(\epsilon^S_L)b_{qL}T G_m(a)\bigr)\eta^T_{G_mM}.$$
The transpose of a map $h:TX\to Y$ is $p(h)\eta^T_X$. Hence the scalar transpose of the left side is $G_n(\epsilon^S_L)b_{qL}TG_m(a)$. Naturality of $b$ rewrites this as
$$G_n(\epsilon^S_L)G_n(Sa)b_M=G_n(\epsilon^S_L\circ Sa)b_M=G_n(a^\sharp)b_M,$$
since the other scalar adjunction gives $a^\sharp=\epsilon^S_L\circ Sa$. This proves the asserted identity for arbitrary $M,L,a$.

Apply the coherent-section theorem to $N$. Under its specified evaluation isomorphisms the extension-form transition is
$$t^{GN}_{m,n}=G_n(t^N_{m,n})\circ b_{N_m}.$$
By construction of the reduction maps from semilinear transitions, $t^N_{m,n}=(a^N_{m,n})^\sharp$ and $t^{GN}_{m,n}=(a^{GN}_{m,n})^\sharp$. Step 4 with $M=N_m$, $L=N_n$, $a=a^N_{m,n}$ identifies the displayed right side with $(\delta_{N_n}G_m(a^N_{m,n}))^\sharp$. Injectivity of the scalar adjunction bijection now yields $a^{GN}_{m,n}=\delta_{N_n}\circ G_m(a^N_{m,n})$. This proves equality of these actual evaluated transition maps without using joint faithfulness of evaluation on arbitrary system-derived morphisms.

For the normalization, take a K-injective $C_n$-complex $I$ and a K-injective replacement $j:qI\to H$ over $C_m$. Apply the normalized direct-image composition comparison to the factorization through $(V,C_m)$. Its representative is $u_*qI\xrightarrow{u_*j}u_*H$. For the other factorization, restriction $p$ is exact and its derived functor is termwise restriction, so its source is canonically $pu_*I=u_*qI$. Thus the comparison between these two factorizations is $d_{QI}=[u_*j]$ under the canonical identifications. Inverting gives exactly the normalization of $\delta$ in the statement. The quoted composition theorem supplies that this representative is a quasi-isomorphism. All comparisons and adjunction bijections used above are natural, so the resulting formula is natural in $N$. When $m=n$ the coefficient morphisms and their pullback comparisons are identities; identity compatibility of composition adjunctions gives $\delta=1$, and both transition maps are identities. The argument nowhere restricts the tower maps to be flat or $N$ to be normalized, and makes no claim that $q$ or $e_n$ preserves K-injectives.
